# screencappy

> screencappy is a free, open source (Apache-2.0) Chrome extension that captures full page screenshots in one click, annotates them, and exports to PNG, JPEG, WebP or PDF. Everything runs locally: no account, no cloud upload, no analytics, and no network code of any kind. screencappy asks for no access to any website, so it cannot see any web page until the moment you ask it to take a screenshot.

screencappy is an alternative to GoFullPage and similar full page screenshot extensions. Features that are commonly paid upgrades elsewhere (annotation, blur and pixelate redaction, emoji stamps, PDF export) are included at no cost. Every feature is free: no trial, no upgrade prompts, no watermarks.

Four ways to capture: Full page (Alt+Shift+P), the entire page including everything you would have to scroll to see. Visible area (Alt+Shift+V), just what is on your screen right now. Select an area (Alt+Shift+S), drag a box around what you want, and you can keep scrolling while you drag to grab something taller than your screen. Pick one thing, which highlights whatever is under the cursor as you move it, so a click captures exactly that photo, table or post with nothing around it.

Capture engines: "Scroll and stitch" is the default. It scrolls the page, takes a picture at each step and joins them into one tall image, using only the access your click grants and asking for no access to any website. Menus and banners that normally follow you as you scroll appear just once, including ones nested inside a page's own self contained components; it also handles parallax backgrounds, waits for photos to finish loading, hides scrollbars, and copes with animations, high resolution screens and browser zoom. "Turbo" is opt in at the engine level, captures in one shot via the Chrome DevTools Protocol, and uses the debugger permission. Chrome shows its "started debugging this browser" banner for the duration of a Turbo capture.

Difficult pages: when the window barely scrolls and the real content lives in an inner panel, as in Gmail style apps, screencappy finds that panel and captures all of it. An iframe picked with Pick one thing is captured in full rather than only the part showing inside its box. With auto load enabled, feeds that load more as you scroll are scrolled to the bottom, within a height and time budget, before the capture is taken. A start delay is available for captures that need a menu open or a hover state held. When a page reports a height that makes a full capture impossible, screencappy says so and offers a choice rather than quietly returning half a picture.

Editor: crop, arrows, lines, rectangles, ellipses, freehand pen, highlighter, text, emoji stamps, and blur or pixelate redaction, on a single row of tools with the colour choices in a popover. Nothing you draw is burnt into the image, so anything can be moved or deleted later, with full undo and redo, zoom and pan.

Export: PNG, JPEG, WebP, PDF (single tall page, or paginated to A4 or Letter), or straight to the clipboard. With the Turbo engine switched on, screencappy can also print the live page to a PDF with real selectable and searchable text. Filename templates such as {domain} {date} {time}. Captures larger than the size limit browsers put on a single image are stored as strips and split automatically across numbered files or extra PDF pages instead of failing. A capture can also be sent straight to your downloads without the editor opening, for when saving is all you want.

Mobile widths: a mobile capture option reflows the page to a phone width layout through device emulation and captures the full mobile page, without resizing the real browser window. The emulated width is configurable.

History: recent captures, with their annotations, are kept locally in IndexedDB with thumbnails. Prune limits are configurable. Nothing syncs anywhere.

Permissions: activeTab, scripting, storage, downloads, contextMenus, unlimitedStorage and debugger. The headline is that screencappy asks for no access to any website: it cannot see any web page until the moment you ask it to take a screenshot, and that access covers one tab, at that moment. Chrome does not allow debugger to be an optional permission, so it is declared at install rather than requested later. It powers the Turbo engine, the mobile width capture and the searchable PDF export, it is only active while one of those captures is running, and Chrome shows a visible banner the whole time it is in use. The Firefox build strips the permission entirely, and the store build ships without it too, leaving the other six.

Browsers: screencappy works with Chrome, Edge, Opera and Brave, which run the same build with every feature available. It is also available for Firefox; that build runs the scroll and stitch engine only, because Firefox has no debugger API.

Installing: store listings are not live yet. screencappy is on its way to the Chrome Web Store, and until it lands the install path is the packaged build attached to each GitHub release, offered on the site as clearly labelled early access. Download screencappy.zip (or screencappy-firefox.zip for Firefox) from the latest release, unzip it, open chrome://extensions, switch on Developer mode, click Load unpacked, and choose the unzipped folder. It takes about a minute.

Licence and author: Apache-2.0, built and maintained by Aaron Pinto, developed in the open.

## Docs

- [Home](https://screencappy.smollet.app/): What screencappy is, its features, and how to install it
- [FAQ](https://screencappy.smollet.app/faq): Answers on install, permissions, privacy, export formats, browser support, and licence
- [How to take a full page screenshot in Chrome](https://screencappy.smollet.app/how-to-take-a-full-page-screenshot-in-chrome): The built in DevTools method, its limits, and the one click method
- [Privacy policy](https://screencappy.smollet.app/privacy): What data screencappy handles, which is none that leaves your device

## Comparisons

Every figure on these pages was read from the vendor's own site or Chrome Web Store listing on 15 August 2026, and each page carries that verification date. The set deliberately names the cases where a competitor is the better tool, including two pages that recommend the other product outright and one that recommends installing nothing at all.

- [Full page screenshot tools compared](https://screencappy.smollet.app/alternatives): The hub, sorted by use case rather than by rank, with a summary table of price, licence, account, uploads and annotation
- [GoFullPage alternative](https://screencappy.smollet.app/gofullpage-alternative): Free capture with cropping and annotation behind Premium at $12 USD per year, versus free annotation and public source
- [FireShot alternative](https://screencappy.smollet.app/fireshot-alternative): The widest format and browser support in the set, at $39.95 per year or $99.95 once, with most of the editor available on Windows only
- [Awesome Screenshot alternative](https://screencappy.smollet.app/awesome-screenshot-alternative): A cloud and team platform from $6 per month that requires an account, versus local only capture with none
- [Nimbus Screenshot alternative](https://screencappy.smollet.app/nimbus-screenshot-alternative): Now FuseBase Capture, an account required collaboration platform with two live pricing surfaces that do not reconcile
- [CocoShot alternative](https://screencappy.smollet.app/cocoshot-alternative): The closest match in the set, both free and account free, differing on open source and on what access each one asks for
- [Screenity and screencappy](https://screencappy.smollet.app/screenity-alternative): Disambiguation. Screenity is a free GPL-3.0 screen recorder that takes no screenshots at all
- [SingleFile and screencappy](https://screencappy.smollet.app/singlefile-alternative): Disambiguation. SingleFile saves a page as one self contained HTML file with selectable text, not as an image
- [Full page screenshots without an extension](https://screencappy.smollet.app/chrome-full-page-screenshot-without-extension): Chrome's DevTools route and Firefox's built in capture, and the advice to install nothing if you only need this occasionally
